critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: The localization rule did not specify the container top-face height or which visible face corners to use to recover its grasp-axis center. Here the red cube's upper-left covering container was correctly selected, but its center was estimated about 1 cm too far in both +x and +y. Specify the top-face plane height and calibrated corner-based center reconstruction so the approach is centered at approximately x=-0.1434, y=-0.1639, z=0.20, rather than using the visible silhouette center.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
At the initial open-hand approach to the container hiding the requested red cube, the retained uncovered/covered demonstration pair correctly identified the target. However, the policy placed the approach about a centimetre too far in both positive x and positive y. The memory was correct; the instruction to account for top-face height without specifying that plane or the relevant corners left metric localization underspecified, breaking SUFFICIENCY.

Replace the vague container-center estimation rule with calibrated top-face reconstruction. For a resting container, use the upper horizontal square face, approximately z=0.05 m above the table, not the whole visible silhouette, the lower rim, or the grasp TCP height. Identify the four outer corners of that horizontal face, excluding visible vertical side faces. Back-project their pixels using the camera intrinsics and world-to-camera extrinsics, intersect each world-space ray with the z=0.05 m plane, and average the reconstructed corners to obtain the grasp-axis x,y. Recover yaw from the reconstructed square edges, choosing the equivalent alignment closest to zero. Where corners are partially obscured, fit the square to its visible edges and check against the other calibrated view rather than averaging the silhouette. Use the current wrist camera calibration when reconstructing from that view.

Command the open-hand approach at that reconstructed x,y and z=0.20 m. At approach height, reconstruct the same face again from the current wrist image to correct lateral undershoot, then descend directly to z=0.0634 m and close. The top-face reconstruction plane and the TCP grasp height are distinct. Retain the existing target-association, lift, replacement, and clearance rules; no additional memory field or episode-specific coordinate is needed.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Estimate container center and orientation using calibrated image geometry, preferably its top-face corners and the wrist view. Account for the height of the top face rather than projecting its center onto the tabletop.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Localize a resting container by reconstructing its upper horizontal square face on the world z=0.05 m plane. Identify that face's four outer corners, excluding vertical side faces and the lower rim; do not use the whole silhouette or the grasp TCP height as the reconstruction plane. For each corner pixel p=(u,v,1), compute the camera center C=-R^T t and world ray d=R^T K^{-1}p using the view's calibration. Intersect the ray with the face plane: X=C+((0.05-C_z)/d_z)d. Average the four reconstructed corners to obtain the grasp-axis x,y, and recover yaw from the reconstructed square edges. If corners are obscured, fit the square to visible top-face edges and check against the other calibrated view rather than averaging the silhouette. Use the current wrist-camera extrinsics for the wrist view. Command the open-hand approach at this reconstructed x,y and z=0.20 m.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Use visible geometry to correct lateral approach error without inserting an extra approach waypoint.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: At approach height, reconstruct the same top face again using the current calibrated wrist image, checked against the front view, to correct lateral undershoot. Descend directly to the reconstructed x,y at the grasp TCP height and close, without inserting an extra approach waypoint. The z=0.05 m reconstruction plane is distinct from the z=0.0633 m grasp TCP height.

fields.name: demonstration_reference
fields.description: At the video cycle, store an ordered pair of frame labels: the last frame showing the uncovered colored cubes, followed by the first frame showing the settled containers covering them. Retain this pair throughout execution. These images preserve the color-to-container correspondence, including targets obscured by the hand later. e.g. ["V16", "V32"]
fields.annotation: At the video cycle, store an ordered pair of frame labels: the last frame showing the uncovered colored cubes, followed by the first frame showing the settled containers covering them. Retain this pair throughout execution. These images preserve the color-to-container correspondence, including targets obscured by the hand later. e.g. ["V16", "V32"]

fields.name: completed_lifts
fields.description: Write zero at the video cycle. At an act cycle, increment the incoming count once only if this cycle's motion images show the closed hand lifting the next requested container from near z=0.063 m to near z=0.20 m, with the container moving with the hand and its cube exposed. A stationary elevated grasp or a downward motion is not another lift. Otherwise copy the incoming count, including after release and retreat. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Initialize to zero at the video cycle. Increment once at the act cycle showing a requested container successfully raised from grasp height to approximately z=0.20 m while held closed, exposing its cube. Count requested containers in instruction order. Do not increment on approach, grasp closure, lowering, release, or retreat. Retain the count otherwise. e.g. 1

texts.action:
At the video cycle write memory only. Execution begins with an open hand high above the table. Read the requested colors in instruction order and use demonstration_reference to associate each with its covering container. Match the uncovered cube locations to the covering events and settled arrangement, not to arbitrary container ordering; ignore extra containers. Use the current images to localize the corresponding container. Front-image right is positive world y.

Localize a resting container by reconstructing its upper horizontal square face on the world z=0.05 m plane. Identify that face's four outer corners, excluding vertical side faces and the lower rim; do not use the whole silhouette or the grasp TCP height as the reconstruction plane. For each corner pixel p=(u,v,1), compute the camera center C=-R^T t and world ray d=R^T K^{-1}p using the view's calibration. Intersect the ray with the face plane: X=C+((0.05-C_z)/d_z)d. Average the four reconstructed corners to obtain the grasp-axis x,y, and recover yaw from the reconstructed square edges. If corners are obscured, fit the square to visible top-face edges and check against the other calibrated view rather than averaging the silhouette. Use the current wrist-camera extrinsics for the wrist view. Command the open-hand approach at this reconstructed x,y and z=0.20 m. Use a downward hand, roll=3.1416 and pitch=0, with yaw aligned to the container's square sides, choosing the equivalent yaw closest to zero. Container grasp TCP height is approximately 0.0633 m. Approach and lift height is 0.20 m. Re-estimate the actual container center rather than using the achieved TCP x,y blindly: approach motions can undershoot by more than a centimetre.

Apply these state-dependent rules, using completed_lifts updated from the motion just observed:

If the hand is closed around a container at low grasp height, lift that container to z=0.20 with the gripper closed. Center the lift over the container's current x,y, preserving its aligned yaw. This rule takes precedence over selecting another target.

If a completed requested lift leaves a container held at z approximately 0.20 and further requested colors remain, lower it vertically at the current TCP x,y to z=0.070 and open the gripper at arrival; preserve the current orientation. Do not carry it to the next target or drop it from approach height.

If the gripper is open near z=0.070 following that replacement, retreat vertically at the current x,y to z=0.146 with the gripper open and orientation preserved. The next target is not approached laterally until this clearance is reached.

Otherwise, with an empty open hand, select requested color number completed_lifts+1. If not already above that container at approximately z=0.20, move to its center x,y at z=0.20 with aligned downward orientation and the gripper open. This includes the initial high pose and the post-release clearance pose. If already above the selected container at approach height, descend to its center x,y at z=0.0633 and close at arrival. At approach height, reconstruct the same top face again using the current calibrated wrist image, checked against the front view, to correct lateral undershoot. Descend directly to the reconstructed x,y at the grasp TCP height and close, without inserting an extra approach waypoint. The z=0.05 m reconstruction plane is distinct from the z=0.0633 m grasp TCP height.

After the final requested lift, keep holding the container; do not replace it. If another cycle arrives despite completion, wait briefly with the grasp unchanged.

For an ambiguous view, use the retained demonstration images and current wrist image together; do not guess a different container from proximity alone. If localization remains uncertain, make a safe open-hand upward clearance move before reassessing, or briefly wait if holding an object. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint; any necessary gripper-only change must include at least 0.002 m of safe motion. If an action executed no steps, do not infer progress or increment the lift count.
